releases.name: v1.1.1
releases.body:
The latest release of Hades (v1.1.0) went out smoothly overall, but a rather significant issue slipped through and required a quick patch release to address it 😬.

Below is a short summary of what’s included in this new release:

 - Fixed an issue where gamepad bindings were not properly saved to the configuration file.
 - Added support and official builds for Windows ARM64 (thanks to [@tordona](https://github.com/tordona) 🙌)
 - Introduced a new shortcut to quickly focus the menu bar.
 - Improved gamepad support to make navigating the UI with only a gamepad smoother and more intuitive.
 
You can find a complete changelog with more details [on our blog](https://hades-emu.org/blog/release-1.1.1/)!

Download instructions are available [here](https://hades-emu.org/download/).

Thank you for taking the time to check on Hades~

I am proud to announce the first release of Hades, version 1.0.0!

This first release provides:

  - A complete emulation of the Game Boy Advance (with the exception of most external devices and add-ons)
  - Decent accuracy
  - Game controller support
  - Keys and buttons remapping
  - Quick Saves (also known as Save State)
  - Real Time Clock (RTC) support
  - Color correction & LCD effects
  - Loading games from common archive formats (.zip, .7z, .rar, etc.)

I will now focus my efforts on performances, accuracy and providing support for more video effects and new external devices!

Than you for taking the time to check on Hades~

releases.name: v1.1.34
releases.body:
**Fixed: the picture on foldables and nearly square screens** ([#66](https://github.com/bhuiyah/ff7-recomp-android/issues/66))

On a screen narrower than the game's picture, like a Galaxy Z Fold's inner screen, the game was stretched to fill the whole screen, so every aspect ratio setting looked the same. The picture now keeps its shape, with black bars above and below. **4:3** and **16:9** look different there now.

- Folding or unfolding the phone while playing now redraws the picture for the new screen. Before, it kept the shape of the screen the game started on.
- The on-screen controls now keep a separate size and layout for nearly square screens (a foldable's inner screen) and for ordinary ones. Change them in **Settings → On-screen controls → Size and layout** on each screen. The game switches between them when you fold or unfold.

Tested on an AYN Thor with its screen set to a nearly square size, at start and mid-game, in 4:3 and 16:9, and back again.

### Updating
Go to **Settings → Updates** in the launcher (or install this APK over your current version), then press **Play**. The launcher asks to **Update the game** once; press it, then **Play**.

releases.name: v1.1.33
releases.body:
**New: "60 FPS, battles at 30" frame rate** ([#64](https://github.com/bhuiyah/ff7-recomp-android/issues/64))

Some phones hold 60 FPS walking around but slow down in battle. This new choice runs the field, world map and minigames at 60 and battles at a steady 30, using the same battle settings as the "30 FPS battles" mode.

- Go to **Settings → Frame rate** and pick **60 FPS, battles at 30**.
- Save states keep working within the same frame-rate choice, as before.

Tested on an AYN Thor with 8 mods: the field ran at 60.0 FPS, the first battle at 30.0 FPS, and the field was back at 60 after the victory.

Also: the README now says not to install the **60/30 FPS Gameplay** mod, which doesn't work with FF7Recomp. Use **Settings → Frame rate** instead ([#63](https://github.com/bhuiyah/ff7-recomp-android/issues/63)).

### Updating
Go to **Settings → Updates** in the launcher (or install this APK over your current version), then press **Play**. The launcher asks to **Update the game** once; press it, then **Play**.

releases.name: v1.1.32
releases.body:
**New: right analog stick, L3 and R3 on the on-screen controls** ([#62](https://github.com/bhuiyah/ff7-recomp-android/issues/62))

Playing with the touch controls, there was no way to turn the battle camera or use FFNx's L3 shortcuts (L3 then R1 / L1 for game speed, and so on). Now there is:

- Go to **Settings → On-screen controls → Size and layout…** and tick **Right stick, L3 and R3**.
- An analog **right stick** appears above the face buttons. Put a finger on it and slide: it works like a controller's right stick. With **Settings → Controller → Analog stick** on, it turns the camera in battles.
- **L3** and **R3** appear under SELECT and START. Press L3, then a shoulder button, for FFNx's shortcuts.
- The stick is its own group, so you can drag it somewhere else in the same screen, like the D-pad and the other buttons.
- It's off by default, so your current layout looks the same until you turn it on.

Tested on an AYN Thor: L3 opened FFNx's shortcut mode ("Waiting for shortcut input.."), and holding the on-screen stick turned the camera during the first battle.

### Updating

releases.name: v1.1.31
releases.body:
**New: keep your game files, mods and saves in a folder you choose** ([#61](https://github.com/bhuiyah/ff7-recomp-android/issues/61))

Until now everything lived in the app's own `Android/data/com.ff7recomp/files` folder (in internal storage or on the SD card). Other apps, file managers and sync tools like Syncthing often can't get into that folder, so it was awkward to back up or sync.

**Settings → Storage → Custom folder** now lets you pick any folder on the device or the SD card, such as `/sdcard/FF7Recomp` or `/sdcard/PC Games/ff7`:

- The first time, Android asks you to turn on **All files access** for FF7Recomp. Apps need that permission to use folders outside their own. FF7Recomp only asks for it when you choose a custom folder.
- **An empty folder** (or a new one you create in the picker): your game files, mods, saves and save states move into it. The launcher restarts when the move is done.
- **A folder that already holds FF7Recomp's files** (a backup, a synced copy, or files from another device): the launcher offers to use them as they are. Your current files stay where they were.

releases.name: v1.1.30
releases.body:
**Fixed: Android closing the game while you use Pixel Guide (or another app) on the bottom screen** ([#59](https://github.com/bhuiyah/ff7-recomp-android/issues/59))

When you touch or scroll an app on the bottom screen, Android treats that app as the one in front, and the game on the top screen becomes less important to it. If the device then ran low on memory, Android's low-memory cleanup closed the game first, because it was the biggest app it could close, even though you were still playing it.

Now, when Android reports that memory is running low while another app is in front on the other screen, the game puts itself back in front. It stays open, the controller plays it again, and the other app is cleaned up before the game. Pixel Guide stays on the bottom screen where you left it.

Tested on an AYN Thor with the reporter's texture mods: with Pixel Guide open and scrolled on the bottom screen, the game was ranked below it; after Android's low-memory signal, the game was back in front with Pixel Guide still showing. The game's own memory stayed steady through fields and battles, so this wasn't a leak in the game.

### Updating

New audio, rendering, and Android startup fixes are here. Huge thanks to

The debug APK is for users of the separate developer app.

Older QA and developer builds used the main app's update address. Install the
matching v2.1 APK once, without uninstalling. From this version onward, each
app receives updates for its own package only.

## What changed

releases.name: Skate 3 Mobile v2.0.18 QA 7
releases.body:
# Skate 3 Mobile v2.0.18 QA 7

This QA build targets startup hangs on the AYN Thor and Retroid Pocket 5.

- Android now keeps the boot frontend and startup movies on the complete emulated presentation path.
- Native Vulkan pipeline compilation waits until the game has actually queued world content.
- A false boot-time gameplay signal can no longer switch the following EA movie into native loading mode.
- A four-second watchdog completes only the first continuously stuck frontend movie. Later career movies are not affected.
- The stable app and stable update channel remain unchanged.

Use the System Driver first. Fully close the QA app between attempts and test at least five cold launches. On a successful test, confirm that you reached gameplay. On a failed test, attach the launcher diagnostics and full log to the existing device issue.

The APK includes no game data.

## Português do Brasil

releases.name: Skate 3 Mobile v2.0.18 QA 6
releases.body:
# Skate 3 Mobile v2.0.18 QA 6

This QA build targets an intermittent early-boot hang reported on the Retroid Pocket 5.

The failed QA 5 diagnostic showed a live audio thread but no first presentation, native pipeline creation, scene target, or crash. The guest render thread stopped immediately after its first offscreen 2D captures.

QA 6 tightens the boot capture boundary:

- Only the four verified 2D vertex layouts and three supported primitive types are accepted.
- Individual and per-frame 2D payloads have conservative size limits.
- Invalid transient draw state is rejected before reading guest memory.
- The first twelve guest frames now log capture begin and completion markers.

Install QA 6 over the previous QA app, keep the System Driver selected, fully close the app between attempts, and test at least five launches. Attach diagnostics from any failed launch.

The stable app and stable update channel are unchanged. The APK includes no game data.

## Português do Brasil

releases.name: Skate 3 Mobile v2.0.18 QA 5
releases.body:
# Skate 3 Mobile v2.0.18 QA 5

This is an opt-in diagnostic build that installs over earlier **Skate 3 QA** builds and preserves QA app data.

## RP5 intermittent black-screen fix

QA 4 proved that the Retroid Pocket 5 can render the Quality profile's 1280x720 scene target, but testers reported that startup only succeeded roughly half the time.

The QA 4 profile copied Performance's visible feature settings, but one internal pipeline gate still used the profile number. Quality therefore compiled optional outline, spline, and shadow shader families even though those features were disabled. Cold and partially warmed shader caches could take different startup paths.

QA 5 fixes the mismatch:

- The 1280x720 Quality target remains enabled.
- The pipeline builder now follows the active lean-scene flag instead of assuming every Quality profile needs the full optional PSO set.
- Renderer installation applies the same defensive lean-feature guard.
- The startup log must report `lean Android set` for this QA Quality profile.
- Stable v2.0.17 and its update channel remain unchanged.

## RP5 test

1. Install QA 5 directly over QA 4.
2. Keep the System Driver selected.

releases.name: DolphinVR Redux v0.5 - The Fall Update
releases.body:
DolphinVR Redux v0.5 brings VR game patches, which put your hands and your head into the games themselves, an in-game menu you use without taking the headset off, a large round of Meta Quest performance work, and automatic updates on Windows.

## Highlights

- **VR game patches.** The arm cannon follows your controller in the Metroid Prime games, the gun and sword follow it in Red Steel 1 and 2, Skyward Sword reads your controller's true pose, and Twilight Princess, The Wind Waker, Wii Sports and Shadow the Hedgehog can be played in first person.
- **An in-game VR menu.** Click the left thumbstick during a game to pause, fast forward, change settings, rebind controls, manage savestates and hunt overrides, all inside the headset.
- **Faster on Meta Quest.** Super Mario Galaxy went from 42 to 60 fps and Super Mario Sunshine from 49 to 60 fps at native resolution in my tests with "Smart Foveation EFB".
- **Automatic updates on Windows.** This is the first version that updates itself. See "Installing" below.
- **Rebased on the latest Dolphin** development builds (October 2026).

## VR game patches

releases.name: DolphinVR Redux v0.4 — The Summer Update

OpenXR and VR

- Added a new VR configuration panel for controller bindings.
- Added new camera and controller anchor overrides.
- Added a new "Screen pane" override.
- Updated the Wiimote pointer to use absolute pointing.
- Fixed Wii MotionPlus gyroscope behavior.

Meta Quest

- Added passthrough support for Meta Quest headsets.
- Added foveated rendering to improve performance.
- Added a new first-launch screen for applying recommended Quest bindings.

releases.name: Dolphin VR Redux v0.3 — The Metroid Update
releases.body:
This update brings a major round of improvements, with a strong focus on Metroid Prime, element overrides, Vulkan rendering, and overall performance.

- All major Metroid Prime fixes from the 2016 DolphinVR-Hydra branch have now been ported and integrated, including: Detect Skybox, Remove Cinematic Bars, 3D HUD, Visor EFB Skips...

releases.name: v2.5.17 — Microsoft sign-in
releases.body:
## What's new

- **Microsoft sign-in no longer opens a blank white page** ([#3](https://github.com/FlameLaunchers/FlameLauncher-Android/issues/3)). Android's WebView puts `; wv` in its user agent, Microsoft reads that as an embedded browser and refuses the page — and what you get is not a message, it is an empty white screen. The marker is gone from the user agent now.

  Two more things the sign-in page needs were missing: cross-site cookies, which `login.live.com` relies on, and a `WebChromeClient`, without which the popups and dialogs the flow opens are silently dropped. The iOS build never hit any of this because WKWebView reports itself as Safari and handles those by default.
- **A sign-in page that fails to load now says why.** Main-frame errors were going nowhere, so a failure left the same white screen with nothing to report.

releases.name: v2.5.16 — Minecraft 26.4 snapshots
releases.body:
## What's new

- **Minecraft 26.4 snapshots start.** A version id like `26.4-snapshot-3` splits into `26` and `4-snapshot-3`, and reading that second part as a plain integer gave nothing — so 26.4 was treated as 26.0, missed the SDL and LWJGL 3.4.3 stack, and launched on LWJGL 3.3.6 instead. The game died immediately with `NoClassDefFoundError: org/lwjgl/sdl/SDLPlatform`; the cacio lines in the crash report were a consequence, not the cause. Version numbers are now read digit by digit, so snapshot, pre-release and rc suffixes no longer hide them, and five tests cover the shapes.
- Carries the previous fix as well: on Java 24 and newer the cacio java agent is skipped, because the `sun.misc.Unsafe` calls its `premain` depends on are refused there and a failing agent takes the VM with it.

releases.name: v2.5.15 — Minecraft 26.4 starts again
releases.body:
## What's new

- **Minecraft 26.4 (and anything else on Java 24 or newer) starts again.** The cacio setup loaded a java agent whose `premain` overwrites the AWT toolkit's static fields through `sun.misc.Unsafe` (`staticFieldBase`, `staticFieldOffset`, `putObject`). Those methods are refused from JDK 24 and gone in 26, and a failing agent takes the whole VM down with it — which surfaced as a cacio error at startup.

  The iOS build has always run the same cacio jars without that agent, on the same Java 25, using only `-Dawt.toolkit` and `-Xbootclasspath/a`. Android now does the same on Java 24+ and keeps the agent only for the older runtimes that still need it.

# Model 3-Vulkan v0.9.9.8 — Release Notes

**2026-11-14 · Windows x64 · Linux x86_64 · macOS Intel**

Model 3-Vulkan v0.9.9.8 is a performance release. Nothing in the emulation model changed: every
game still renders the same picture it did in v0.9.9.6, and the same save states still load. What
changed is how much work the CPU and the GPU have to do to get there.

The headline is that the hybrid JIT now translates **more than 80 % of the guest instruction
stream to native x86-64**, the Vulkan renderer stopped paying for a redundant depth write that was
silently disabling hardware Early-Z / Hi-Z culling, and UMA GPUs finally get zero-copy geometry
upload. Together those turn the integrated-GPU experience from "lock it to 496×384" into a picture
that can actually be played at native resolution.

Windows build is unchanged since v0.9.8.6 and does not need this update.

---

## Fixed in both packages

**The in-game settings panel ignored the mouse and the keyboard on Linux and macOS.**

Press Tab and the panel opened, but nothing in it responded: no hover highlight, no clicks, no arrow
keys, no Enter. The panel's input feed was Windows-only — the whole block that reads the pointer
position, the mouse buttons and the key states sat behind `#ifdef _WIN32`, with no equivalent for the
other platforms, so on Linux and macOS only the mouse wheel was ever delivered. It now reads the
platform's per-frame input snapshot, which both backends already maintain: pointer position, three
mouse buttons, Ctrl/Shift/Alt and a full key table (arrows, Tab, Enter, Escape, Home/End, Page Up/Down,
Insert/Delete, Backspace, Space, A/C/V/X/Z, digits and the keypad).

# Model 3-Vulkan v0.9.9.8 — Release Notes

**2026-11-14 · Windows x64 · Linux x86_64 · macOS Intel**

Model 3-Vulkan v0.9.9.8 is a performance release. Nothing in the emulation model changed: every
game still renders the same picture it did in v0.9.9.6, and the same save states still load. What
changed is how much work the CPU and the GPU have to do to get there.

stream to native x86-64**, the Vulkan renderer stopped paying for a redundant depth write that was
silently disabling hardware Early-Z / Hi-Z culling, and UMA GPUs finally get zero-copy geometry
upload. Together those turn the integrated-GPU experience from "lock it to 496×384" into a picture
that can actually be played at native resolution.

**Beta, for testing.** Install it by hand, or turn on Include prereleases for Pocket Foundry in Obtainium. It updates to the release once that's out.

releases.body:
**Beta 0.3.4.** Acaba a **queda de fps depois de fechar o inventário** ([#53](https://github.com/mamcjr/TOTKDroid/issues/53), [#24](https://github.com/mamcjr/TOTKDroid/issues/24)) e melhora a **geração de quadros (LSFG)**: importar o `Lossless.dll`, funcionar em mais GPUs Mali e pedir à tela a taxa de atualização que os quadros gerados precisam.

> **Nenhum arquivo do jogo vem junto.** Você precisa do seu próprio dump de *Tears of the Kingdom* com a atualização **1.4.3** aplicada (`exefs` e `romfs`, ou o `romfs` como um único `romfs.bin`).

Atualiza por cima das versões anteriores sem apagar os saves. **Não desinstale o app antes**: isso apaga os saves.

## O que mudou

- **Queda depois do menu ([#53](https://github.com/mamcjr/TOTKDroid/issues/53), [#24](https://github.com/mamcjr/TOTKDroid/issues/24)):**
  - A queda de 12-14 s depois de fechar o inventário, de escolher uma arma ou de salvar não era o clock da GPU, como eu tinha dito.
  - O app desligava o "sync lag" por ~10 s sempre que o jogo saía do mundo, para proteger os carregamentos. Só que ele não distinguia um menu de uma tela de carregamento, e nesses segundos a CPU ficava esperando a GPU.

releases.name: TOTKDroid 0.3.3 (beta): FSR 1 e FXAA mais leves
releases.body:

> **Nenhum arquivo do jogo vem junto.** Você precisa do seu próprio dump de *Tears of the Kingdom* com a atualização **1.4.3** aplicada (`exefs` e `romfs`, ou o `romfs` como um único `romfs.bin`).

Atualiza por cima das versões anteriores sem apagar os saves. **Não desinstale o app antes**: isso apaga os saves.

## O que mudou

- **FSR 1 (EASU) na metade do tempo:**
  - A análise de borda roda uma vez por pixel, em vez de quatro.
  - Onde não há borda, o pixel sai direto da interpolação bilinear.
  - As contas de cor usam meia precisão, que vira fp16 onde o driver aceita.
  - No POCO F7 Ultra (Adreno 830), o upscale de 1280x717 para 1920x1080 caiu de 1,00 para 0,50 ms por quadro. Não vi diferença nas bordas lado a lado.
  - Ideias do artigo "Optimizing FSR", de atyuwen, reescritas a partir do FSR 1 original.
- **FXAA ~18% mais leve:**
  - Usa meia precisão e o limiar padrão do FXAA 3.11, em vez do "ultra".
  - A busca da borda é mais curta: 5 passos em vez de 10.
  - No POCO caiu de 0,51-0,59 para 0,43-0,44 ms por quadro, sem diferença de serrilhado visível.

Release Notes for openMSX 22.0 (2026-10-28)
===========================================

Thanks to many contributors (who make good use of modern AI tools), we
have a very long list of changes again. Major features are found in the
debugger GUI, with a new Raster Beam Viewer and Tracer functionality. We also
have the Quick Setup Editor, for one-window access to all major setup
settings.

came with Konami's A1 Spirit), light guns, Franky, Makoto, SD Mapper V1 and
SM-X WiFi. There's even a synthetic TCP/IP UNAPI device to be able to try out
network programs in openMSX.

And many, many more things...

Special thanks to all the contributors of this release who are not in the core
team! Keep those pull requests coming!

Here's the list with all highlights and details:

MSX device support:
- fixed Yamanooto SCC register visibility

releases.name: openMSX 21.0
releases.body:
openMSX 21.0 has many improvements on the new GUI introduced in openMSX 20.0 (especially the debugger) and several other smaller features. It also introduces the "setups" concept, which enables you to define an MSX setup (e.g. a Philips VG 8020 with an external disk drive and a joystick, data recorder and printer connected). These can be created, loaded, and automatically started. They can also be saved automatically when you exit.

Furthermore, flash chip emulation has become a lot more accurate, thanks to Laurens Holst.

releases.name: openMSX 20.0
releases.body:
openMSX 20.0—Autumn Spring—is a major release, in which we introduce the new Graphical User Interface, replacing the OSD menu. A faster and more powerful debugger is now included in openMSX itself. Configuration for MSX joystick/JoyMega has been improved drastically using the new GUI. If you still want to use Catapult, you can use the Catapult release that came with openMSX 19.0. Please [read the release notes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openMSX/openMSX/RELEASE_20_0/doc/release-notes.txt) for details of the openMSX changes.

As always, special thanks to all the contributors of this release who are not in the core team! Keep these pull requests coming!

Please note that as of now, a system with OpenGL 2 support is required to run openMSX.

releases.name: openMSX 19.1
releases.body:
openMSX 19.1—Reflection—is a bug fix release for openMSX 19.0, as we found some rather nasty issues after releasing, mostly that LaserDisc support was broken. No new Catapult will be released, as it has no changes.  Please [read the release notes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openMSX/openMSX/RELEASE_19_1/doc/release-notes.txt) for details of the openMSX changes.

Thanks for those who gave us the feedback so that we found out about these issues.

Please note that this will be the last openMSX release that supports systems without OpenGL 2 or higher.

releases.body:
> [!NOTE]
> Wondering about your save data when upgrading? Don't worry! Your save data is stored separately to the game itself. You can overwrite your old version and your save data will still be there, completely intact, and will work on the new version.

## Changelog
- Removed B Locker from extended draw distances, fixing a bug with being able to shoot the coconut switch in Hideout Helm lobby on higher draw distances
- Fixed a minor bug with sprite interpolation fixes where the matrix tag index of the sprite would overflow into unintended bounds
- Separated out options for gyro & mouse inversion. As such, you can now independently control which of these are inverted ( #73 )( #79 )
  - This now also impacts the controls of the cannon game in Gloomy Galleon
- Changed how the reduced lightning setting works ( #63 )( #89 )
  - Instead of reducing how intense a lightning strike is, instead it now reduces how frequently the flashes take place

- Added in the ability to boot recomp via a CLI argument ( #55 )

### Bug Fixes
- Fixed an issue where a large spike in CPU load would permanently kill the audio engine until a program restart.
- Fixed an issue where disabled lightning would not work for some lightning events ( #30 )
- Fixed an issue where the game would leave zipper marks on the game during the open zipper animation
- Fixed an issue where the main menu scrolling background would look very weird on expanded HUD ( #42 )

  sometimes with a label: `(Disk 1, Game Disk)`, `(Disk 2 - Courses)`. RomSieve did not read these names as disks of

releases.body:
**Beta for testing.** This is a pre-release: the Windows launcher does not offer it as an update, and Windows players stay on 1.9.8.6.

## Seamless co-op on Linux

`Bloodborne-Linux-x86_64.AppImage` brings SuperMedo Seamless co-op (BBSC: Yharnam Together's co-op, by **CLSAMG22**) to the Linux version: native, no Wine. Make the file executable and open it.

- The launcher has a new **Seamless co-op** tab with its own Play button. The normal Play at the top still starts the normal game, and the Seamless co-op row on the Online page opens the new tab.
- It uses your SuperMedo account from the Online page: sign in there first.
- Host rules: enemies (normal, auto, a bit harder, harder, much harder, or your own health / damage / poise values from 1 to 10), boss tempo, rot, travel together with a vote, revive.
- Russia route for networks that cannot reach the SuperMedo server.
- Its own characters in `~/.local/share/bbport/seamless/user/savedata`, apart from your normal saves. Starting a new game is recommended. Your game folder is not changed: the co-op files are made in `~/.local/share/bbport/seamless`.

releases.name: Bloodborne PC 1.9.8.6
releases.body:
# Bloodborne PC 1.9.8.6

What's new since 1.9.8.4.

## Picture fixes
- **Smeared picture fixed (two causes):**
  - After a load, the game sometimes rewrote a command buffer it had already handed to the GPU. The picture then stayed broken or smeared until the game was restarted. Every submitted command buffer is now copied first (`BB_COPY_GPU_BUFFERS=0` turns this off). The same cause was behind "Unimplemented PM4 type 0" and "PM4 header ... rest of the buffer dropped" in logs.
  - After a start with an empty shader cache, one saved pipeline could be lost for the whole next session. The game's motion blur then kept blurring the last frame, so the picture looked smeared and frozen from the first camera turn on.
- Rainbow tiles on hit enemies and a light line along the top in cutscenes are fixed.

# Winlator 中文版 (Wine 11) v1.0.0

基于 [Winlator 11.1](https://github.com/brunodev85/winlator) 深度定制:

## 主要变化
- **Wine 10.10 -> Wine 11.15**: 移植 brunodev85 全部定制补丁 (Android 存储符号链接、GPU 信息上报、X11 窗口属性等) 至 Wine 11.15 新 WoW64 模式 (x86_64-unix + i386/x86_64 双架构 PE)
- **esync -> fastsync**: 移除旧 esync 机制, 使用 Wine 11 原生 fastsync, 同步性能更好
- **完整中文支持**:
  - Android 界面全面中文翻译 (values-zh-rCN)
  - 内置 Noto Sans CJK SC 中文字体 + fontconfig 中文别名
  - rootfs 注入 zh_CN.UTF-8 locale (glibc + X11)
  - Wine 前缀注册表中文字体替换 (宋体/SimSun -> Noto Sans CJK SC)
  - 新建容器默认中文环境

## 下载安装
直接下载下方 APK (约 325 MB) 安装即可, 无需额外组件。首次启动会自动解包 rootfs。

## 技术说明
- APK 为 debug 签名, 与官方 Winlator 签名不同, 两者不可互相覆盖安装
- 由 GitHub Actions 全自动云端编译: Wine (约 50 分钟) -> rootfs 注入中文化 -> Gradle 打包
- 构建配方见仓库 `wine/`、`chinese/`、`.github/workflows/build.yml`

releases.name: Ymir v0.4.0
releases.body:
# Ymir v0.4.0
[Discord](https://discord.gg/NN3A7n5dzn) | [Patreon](https://www.patreon.com/StrikerX3) | [Compatibility list](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SLZzL9LelSlpEmTKy8cjaQnE7mew2uW1rfCgcekO58Q/edit?usp=sharing) | [Screenshots](https://emu.layle.dev/ymir/54fead6/)

SDL Renderer has been the backbone of graphics on Ymir... until now. Ymir now supports Direct3D 12 and Metal (with Vulkan to come in the future), which will enable implementation of shaders and resolution scaling down the line. Direct3D 12 also supports hardware-accelerated VDP rendering, offloading heavy graphics computations to your GPU for a significant performance boost with no accuracy compromises -- it's as accurate as the software renderer, save for undiscovered bugs. Other graphics backends will eventually support acceleration as well, hang tight!

The Virtua Gun has been promoted to a stable feature after numerous bug fixes and accuracy improvements that made it work flawlessly with most supported games. Known issues are listed in #787: only one game doesn't register shots, and three don't recognize reloads consistently.

releases.body:
# Ymir v0.3.2
[Discord](https://discord.gg/NN3A7n5dzn) | [Patreon](https://www.patreon.com/StrikerX3) | [Compatibility list](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SLZzL9LelSlpEmTKy8cjaQnE7mew2uW1rfCgcekO58Q/edit?usp=sharing) | [Screenshots](https://emu.layle.dev/ymir/584dcc1/)

This release brings a large set of bug fixes and accuracy improvements once again guided by @celeriyacon's test ROMs, pushing compatibility to just over 94%! A workaround for 16 games described below would bring this number to 94.6%.

The highlight of this version is the huge set of fixes to CD Block HLE, bringing more parity with the LLE counterpart and improving compatibility and stability with dozens of games. VDP1 fixes also resolved a few longstanding issues and brought some games to life.

Performance got another huge boost in multiple avenues with this version. First, thanks to @SternXD, you can now offload audio processing tasks to another CPU core, freeing up the emulator thread to focus more heavily on the SH-2s and general system logic. This alone can boost performance by up to 25% and possibly more, depending on how much work is put on the SCSP DSP.

# PanProbe 1.3.2

Vulkan conformance and performance probe for the Mesa PanVK driver on Mali GPUs (mali_kbase). It loads the bundled driver, the system Vulkan driver or an imported `.so`, shows what the driver reports, and runs **41** on-device tests.

Bundled drivers:
- `rc5` slot (default): [Mesa PanVK 26.3.1](https://github.com/zenithblue-oss/panvk-kbase-android/releases/tag/panvk-kbase-v26.3.1), `26.3.0-devel (git-795ca7ff3e, p0175, 2026-10-31)`, build 122i, universal Mali v6-v14 (v15 not fully supported).
- `rc4` slot: the RC4 driver (`panvk-kbase-v0.1.0-rc4`), for A/B runs.

Package `dev.zenithblue.panvktest`, versionName 1.3.2, versionCode 21. It updates 1.2.7 and 1.3.x in place.

## What is new since 1.2.7

- Bundles build 122i (26.3.1) in the default slot; the `rc4` slot keeps RC4 for A/B runs.
